title: Home Comfort Financing Make-Up Payments
content:
A borrower who brings a missed or returned installment up to date on a Home Comfort Financing account pays the make-up amount as a one-time payment on the account.

The make-up amount on a fixed-rate account is not fixed until the account carries the closing interest charge for every statement period that has closed.

On a fixed-rate account, then, the make-up amount stands only once the account's records show a closing interest charge for each statement period that has closed; on that condition the amount is fixed, and not before.

## The make-up payment: `submit_makeup_payment_e9bd505b`

**Capability.** `submit_makeup_payment_e9bd505b` lets the borrower make a one-time payment on their own Home Comfort Financing account to bring a missed or returned installment up to date. The payment is drawn today by the method the borrower chooses, posts to the account as a payment line with a new confirmation number, and the balance owed falls by the amount paid; the account stays open.

**How it is invoked.** It is the customer's own tool: the agent unlocks `submit_makeup_payment_e9bd505b` and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it.

**Parameters.**

- `finance_account_id` — reference number of the borrower's financing account the payment is made on, as the agent reads it from the financing account lookup and hands it over.
- `amount` — the amount the borrower pays, in USD, 2 decimal places, always positive, exactly as the agent states it.
- `payment_method` — how the borrower pays; one of:
  - `autopay_ach`: drawn under the borrower's standing automatic-payment authorization;
  - `online_ach`: paid once from a checking or savings account by routing and account number;
  - `debit_card`: paid once with a debit card;
  - `check`: paid by a paper check that has been received;
  - `phone_payment`: keyed in by a customer care agent on the borrower's behalf during a call.

**Return.** The receipt carries `finance_txn_id` (reference number of the payment line), `payment_reference` (confirmation number), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places, the amount paid), `payment_method` (the method used), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD date the payment posted), `account_balance` (USD, 2 decimal places, the balance still owed) and `status`, which is "posted" when the payment is on the account.

## Receipt — illustration (hypothetical values)

A make-up payment of 238.47 by `debit_card` on an account owing $7412.90 comes back with `amount` 238.47, `payment_method` `debit_card`, today's `posted_date`, `account_balance` 7174.43, a new `payment_reference` and `status` "posted". The account remains open.
